_comment: One corpus, two readers. ConversationRecorder (PHP) and ai-bridge-chat.js
(browser) are independent implementations of the same protocol rules, and
every parity bug found in this area came from asserting by hand that they
agree. They do not, reliably, and a reviewer noticing is not a test.
Each scenario is a stream of events and the tool_call blocks both sides
must end up with. Add a scenario when a divergence is found; both suites
pick it up with no further wiring.
Only tool_call blocks are compared, and only the fields both sides model:

scenarios.name: a locally-run tool keeps its name and arguments
a server-resolved tool is recorded once, keeping the CLI's id
the frame supplies arguments the block could not parse
the block wins when its own arguments parsed
parallel calls to one tool do not swap arguments when frames return reversed
parallel truncated calls keep their own raw text rather than borrowing
a server-declared tool the bridge runs locally is kept
the operator's own MCP tool is not claimed by a bridge frame
a frame arriving before its block still yields one call
a frame with no block of its own is recorded on its own
a block the stream never closed keeps its arguments
a nameless tool block is dropped by both
a frame carrying enormous arguments is capped by both
